issues.legal_issue: Interest owed under an independent stay order is not part of the amount required to obtain a final decree in a mortgage-redemption proceeding unless it is included in the preliminary decree or adjudged as a subsequent charge.
material_facts: A preliminary decree in a mortgage-redemption suit specified the amounts payable and provided for future interest, and the mortgagor deposited the amount required by that decree.
While an appeal was pending, a stay order required the mortgagor, under an undertaking, to pay additional interest during the stay period.
The additional interest was not included in the preliminary decree, and no subsequent costs, charges, expenses, or interest were adjudged for payment.
The mortgagor's deposit was short only of the additional interest owed under the undertaking; the shortfall was later made good.
issues.conclusion: The additional interest owed under the undertaking was not part of the amount payable under the preliminary decree or an adjudged subsequent charge. The mortgagor was entitled to a final decree, although the court could insist that the undertaking be honoured before passing it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXXIV, rules 7(1)(c)(i) and (ii), and 8(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a mortgagor seeking a final decree must comply with the preliminary decree and pay any subsequent costs, charges, expenses, and interest adjudged due. Such subsequent amounts must be adjudged before the mortgagor is required to deposit them. An additional-interest obligation arising from an independent stay order and undertaking does not become part of the preliminary-decree amount merely because it is payable; the court may nevertheless insist on performance of the undertaking before passing the final decree. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_proceeding and preliminary_decree_obligations_met and extra_interest_arose_from_independent_stay_undertaking and extra_interest_not_included_in_preliminary_decree and no_subsequent_charges_adjudged

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: The proceeding is a mortgagor's suit to redeem mortgaged property and obtain a final decree.
predicates.preliminary_decree_obligations_met: The mortgagor paid the amounts required by the preliminary decree.
predicates.extra_interest_arose_from_independent_st: The mortgagor undertook to pay additional interest as a condition of obtaining a stay of payment.
predicates.extra_interest_not_included_in_prelimina: The additional interest required by the undertaking was not included in the preliminary decree.
predicates.no_subsequent_charges_adjudged: No subsequent costs, charges, expenses, or interest were adjudged due for payment.

issues.definition: When a mortgagor in a redemption proceeding meets the preliminary decree and no subsequent charges have been adjudged, an additional-interest obligation arising independently from a stay undertaking does not prevent entitlement to a final decree, though the undertaking may still be enforced before that decree is passed.
